findings.message: When the self-sync withdraws a proposal, it sends the stored meta back through `syncProposal` unchanged, including `meta.repoPhases`. Since 094, stored phases are entries of the form `{ at, source }`. `SyncInput.meta` validates `repoPhases` with `repoPhasesInMeta`, which only accepts plain time strings (services.ts:238). So the withdrawal is refused and the whole self-sync run throws. Fix: drop `repoPhases` from the meta that goes back through the service, so the locked-row rule keeps the stored entries. The push's withdrawal at push.ts:150 already avoids this by calling `upsertSpecProposal` directly. Add a test that withdraws a proposal that has recorded repo phases.
findings.scenario: A main proposal FLT-101 has `meta.repoPhases = { proposal: { at: '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z', source: 'main@abc1234' } }`. Its folder is deleted and `sync:specclaw` runs. `planWithdrawals` picks FLT-101, `syncProposal` fails with 'meta.repoPhases: phase times by phase', and the run aborts with nothing withdrawn.

findings.message: When `phases.archived.at` is missing, `releasedAt` falls back to `stamps.at(-1)`. `stamps` is sorted as raw strings before `instant()` runs, so with mixed offsets or formats the last string is not always the latest time, and a string `instant()` rejects can be picked over a valid one. Fix: run each stamp through `instant()`, drop the nulls, then sort the ISO results. The plugin bundle has the same code (`plugins/amax/scripts/read-specclaw.mjs`:93).
findings.scenario: The archived phase has no `at`. The other phase times are '2026-10-17T08:00:00+05:30' (02:30Z) and '2026-10-17T03:00:00Z'. The string sort puts the +05:30 one last, so `releasedAt` is 02:30Z instead of the latest time, 03:00Z.

findings.message: 096 AC-1 now merges every stored phase entry into every later write (`out = { ...before }`). Nothing checks that the stored entries belong to the same change. `upsertSpecProposal` (services.ts:323) passes the row's stored `meta.repoPhases` whatever its `source_ref` or withdrawn state, and `desired()` does the same with `prior`. If a later folder takes the key of a withdrawn proposal, it inherits the old change's Approved, Verified and Archived phases for good, because a read that leaves a phase out no longer clears it. Before 096, a read replaced the set, so the new change's state.json cleaned this up. Fix: keep stored entries only when the stored row is the same change (stored `source_ref` equals `input.sourceRef` and the row is not withdrawn). Otherwise resolve from the read alone. Add a variant test for a reused key, a revived withdrawn row and a renamed dir.
findings.scenario: FLT-050 (`050-old`) reaches verify and archived, then its folder is deleted, so it is withdrawn. Later `050-new` is added with only `proposal` approved. The push upserts FLT-050 with `meta.repoPhases = { proposal, verify, archived }`, and the history of 050-new shows 'Verified in the repo' and 'Archived in the repo' for work it never did.

findings.message: The server reads repo times by two rules. `releasedAt` goes through `instant()`, which accepts a bare date, no offset, or `+0530`. Phase times go through `z.string().datetime({ offset: true })`, both in `repoPhasesInMeta` (the SyncInput refine) and in `isTime`. So one hand-written value is accepted in one field and refused or dropped in the other, and offset forms are stored as sent instead of normalised. The comment on `repoInstant` says the server applies the reader's rule, but that holds only for `releasedAt`. Run phase times through `instant()` on the server too.
findings.scenario: `sync_proposal` is called with `meta.repoPhases.verify = "2026-10-17"` and the call is refused by the meta refine. The same value as a push record's `releasedAt` is stored as 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z.
